candidates.concept: Oral health, disease mechanisms and prevention
candidates.assessment: The strongest full24-course biomedical trial is mechanically feasible and supplies real cell/organ science, mucosal immunity and host–pathogen research, molecular pathology, pharmacology, wet laboratory practice, epidemiology, pain/health psychology and evidence synthesis. These respond substantially to foundations but do not sustain oral biology, caries/periodontal disease, oral assessment and restorative science as an organising subject. Research flexibility cannot turn general biomedicine into documented taught oral-health inquiry. Academic comparability fails, not scheduling or professional licensing.

candidates.concept: Patient wellbeing, compassionate communication and accessible oral care
candidates.assessment: A second whole24-course trial repairs the actual Psycholinguistics offering conflict by using2027h1, and meets all formal rules. Health Psychology covers pain, consultation and treatment decisions; sociology and qualitative interviews address inequality and lived experience; psychopathology, cognition, development, ethics and public persuasion offer complementary substance. Together they implement a general health/patient-experience programme. The oral-care object, oral assessment, dental prevention decisions and treatment planning do not become a sustained academic focus. General compassionate care alone does not establish a programme-level response to dentistry.

candidates.concept: Precise restorative dental work and technical treatment
candidates.assessment: A third feasible24-course trial combines biomedical and research foundations with actual physical/chemical materials labs, mineral and biomineralization chemistry, recycling/material analysis, consumer design and robotic manipulation. These provide meaningful material, design and precision methods, considered on their own evidence. Their objects are environmental chemistry, general consumer prototypes and robot kinematics; they do not combine into restorative oral structure/function, dental materials, endodontic or oral-imaging inquiry. This is a substantive subject gap beyond absent supervised treatment or dental qualification.
